priorBlockerDisposition.evidence: The substantial cyan slab masses, broad turning planes/highlights and subordinate embedded stones accepted as progress in round02 remain readable in all four at128/32.

N/S below the pale ledge now has a distinct tapered mid-blue central stone face and neighboring blue faces, soft turns and restrained defined recesses. The lower construction survives128/32 and the inspected backgrounds/phases instead of reading as blurred grooves on a band. E/W faceted cutface progress is also retained.

observations: The low broad blue/cyan shelf reads as several substantial softly rounded or gently faceted slabs. Broad plane transitions establish the major crown before thin joints; the lavender/teal embedded stones remain secondary. All four facings retain coherent material, scale and registration. Compared with the original flat cyan blank and dark lower band, useful native modeled stone construction is now present.

The sole round02 blocker is resolved. In static-N.png and static-S.png, approximately x85–300,y555–612 below the pale ledge, the lower mass now separates into coherent mid-blue stone faces with soft turning edges and controlled recessed seams. This reads as lower stone construction at logical128cell and phone32cell in supplied and independent repeated captures, across light/gray/dark and CSS phases0/.25/.5/.75. It is a shape/plane/readability improvement, beyond a brightness lift.

Cyan upper surfaces and mid-blue lower faces have clear value separation without a near-black dead band. The broad symmetric lighting reveals volume without a preferred horizontal direction, directional ground shadow, hard white highlight stripe or target-derived halo. The E/W exposed cutfaces retain readable faceted blue stone fields. No clipping, missing facing, floating secondary piece, distracting dark patch or bright alpha fringe was observed.

All inspected same-handed three-middle joins are visibly clean in supplied native/independent sheets and independently reproduced consumer captures. There is no visible port crack, isolated internal cap, bright/dark boundary line or crown step at integer/fractional display phases. Complete native-opaque assembly coverage supports that observation; broad finite-area-light RGB differences are retained and are not represented as full-image identity.

The single-view target remains richer in layered stone shapes and tiny color variations. The current simpler, shallower interpretation supplies the frozen major-volume, readable-body, soft-light, purposeful-detail and all-four repeatability outcomes within the exact finite shelf envelope. Literal target topology, taller pebbles, extra height or its cyan edge fringe are not acceptance requirements.
remainingDifferences: Lower stones and crown slabs are simpler and more rectilinear than the richly layered target, but now have readable mid-blue faces and soft plane transitions at128/32. Shallower relief and smaller embedded pebbles are appropriate to the fixed0.45 native height limit.

The target has denser mottled surface variation and stronger painted edge accents. The restrained native cyan/blue treatment keeps major masses legible and avoids noise/halo; those exact painted details and topology are not required.

True W/E cutplanes remain flat and finite, and renderer/area-light residuals below remain measured. These are compatible with clean inspected joints; no full-image RGB equality or derivative-family/end/corner acceptance is inferred.
